milestone.title: mp autopilot roles + topology — Role enum, RoleConfig resolution, and role-to-pane mapping

intent.outcome: The autopilot system has a stable three-role model (orchestrator / runner / reviewer) with a topology declaration that maps roles into 1, 2, or 3 herdr panes, and the role-config resolution chain (session.json override → mp config.json default → built-in) gives every session a fully resolved per-role config without runtime ambiguity.

problem.description: Today's mp watch only knows runner + coordinator (M149). The new architecture splits the coordinator role into orchestrator (cycle decisions) and reviewer (independent verification), per the lessons from M200/M201/M202/M203 where role-boundary violations and fabricated state happened because one agent wore two hats. The 2-pane topology we agreed on is not `coordinator + runner` (the legacy pattern) but `orchestrator+reviewer on one supervisor pane + runner on its own`; the 1-pane topology absorbs all three into one agent (for tracks). The role config must be resolvable per-session with three sources of truth in priority order, and the topology must declare how roles collapse into panes without ambiguity.

in_scope: Introduce `Role` enum (`Orchestrator`, `Runner`, `Reviewer`) in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/role.rs` (or extend the existing `crates/mp/src/watch/herdr.rs` `Role` if rename is deferred).
Introduce `RoleConfig` struct: model, harness, skill, extras (reuses the existing `RoleConfig` from `crates/mp/src/watch/herdr.rs`).

Resolution chain in priority order: (1) `session.json.roles.<role>.*` (per-session override, A1's schema), (2) `mp config.json` `autopilot.roles.<role>.*` (global default), (3) built-in default. The resolution function returns a typed `ResolvedRoleConfig` and is the only path other code uses to read role config.

Topology enum (`One`, `Two`, `Three`) and the role-to-pane mapping function: 3-pane = `[[O], [R], [V]]`; 2-pane = `[[O, V], [R]]`; 1-pane = `[[O, R, V]]`. The function is pure and testable in isolation.

`mp autopilot config get/set autopilot.{topology,refresh_secs,roles.<role>.{model,harness,skill,extras}}` — the read/write surface for global defaults. `mp autopilot session ...` reads the session-scoped overrides.

Topology-mode tightening of the decision matrix (C3's matrix): 3-pane = full matrix applies; 2-pane = no `ship-with-backlog` path (only `cycle-next` or `escalate`); 1-pane = no independent review (C2's reviewer detector for 1-pane returns a sentinel that C3 interprets as 'ship only').
out_of_scope: The role-enforcement boundary (DENY list, permission policies) — out per the simplification decision; orchestrator verifier (C2) is the safety net.
The lane-notification wire format and verifier — those land in C1 and C2.
Per-role spawn prompts (B2) — separate milestone; B1 only resolves the role config, not the prompt content.
The migration of legacy `coordinator` references to `orchestrator` — that's A2's source-folder plan; B1 introduces the new names and the legacy paths continue to resolve.

acceptance_criteria.description: The `Role` enum has three variants; the `Topology` enum has three variants; the role-to-pane mapping function returns the documented slot pattern for each topology.

RoleConfig resolution applies the three-tier priority correctly: a session.json override beats a config.json default beats a built-in. Empty string overrides are treated as 'not set' (the next tier resolves).

`mp autopilot config get autopilot.topology` returns the current value (or a default); `mp autopilot config set autopilot.topology three-agent` writes it; `mp autopilot config get autopilot.roles.runner.harness` returns the configured harness.

Topology policy returns FullMatrix with four-cycle budget for 3-pane, NoShipWithBacklog with a reduced three-cycle budget for 2-pane, and SingleAgentTrackOnly with a two-cycle budget for 1-pane. Starting a full milestone in 1-pane is rejected unless an explicit recorded review-bypass policy exists.

Legacy `agent.runner` and `agent.coordinator` configuration participates in one documented resolution function: explicit autopilot role override wins, then compatible legacy role fallback, then harness default. Conflicts and unsupported reviewer fallback are typed diagnostics.

design_decisions.choice: Three roles (orchestrator / runner / reviewer); the legacy `coordinator` becomes `orchestrator` everywhere.
design_decisions.rationale: Orchestrator's actual duty is the cycle-decision machine (a manager), not the review work; renaming clarifies the skill-set split that M203's lesson (runner self-completed via `mp reviews pass`) demands.

design_decisions.choice: Topology declares slots, but role independence remains a gate: 3-pane has separate O/R/V; 2-pane combines O+V and therefore forbids ship-with-backlog; 1-pane is restricted to tracks/trivial work and full milestones are rejected by preflight.
design_decisions.rationale: Role collapse is operationally useful, but it cannot silently bypass the repository rule that milestones receive independent review.

design_decisions.choice: Global defaults at `autopilot.roles.<role>.*` and `autopilot.topology` in `mp config.json`; per-drive overrides in `session.json`.
design_decisions.rationale: Reuses the M198 `ui.show_watch_tab` precedent; raul Settings lane exposes them as editable values; CLI users also get the same config surface.
